build_notes: Verified the pre-existing docx/xlsx (Case Study, Data, Facilitator Guide) against the current case.md before building anything new: all three mirror case.md/FACILITATOR.md exactly (rendered word/document.xml text extracted and diffed against the source prose), no facilitator content (balance arguments, trap, twist) leaked into the student Case Study docx, every fee/margin figure in the Case Study and Data workbook stays in fraction/mixed-number form (e.g. $18-3/4, $3-1/8, 15%, 3.5%, $3.68 -- exactly as case.md states them, no decimal coercion), and Data.xlsx ships only raw Appendix A/B/C figures with the D1/D3 answer cells left as '(you compute this in D1/D3)' placeholders, not pre-computed. No fixes were needed there. Built the missing piece: The Referral Cut - Interactive.html, from templates/interactive_shell.html per templates/INTERACTIVE_HTML_CONTRACT.md. All interactive arithmetic runs on a hand-written JS Fraction class (gcd-reduced numerator/denominator pairs, exact add/sub/mul/scale) ported directly from cases/the-referral-cut/sensitivity_model.py's PARAMS/evaluate()/working_capital() -- PARAMS holds every Appendix A/B/C figure as an exact Frac (price 75/4, packaging_cost 25/8, production_cost 13/2, referral_fee 3/20, base_fba_fee 92/25, fuel_surcharge 7/200, etc.), and evaluate()/evaluate_twist()/working_capital() derive post_referral, net_A/net_B, monthly_A/monthly_B, and each option's working capital live, every time, rather than storing any pre-computed verdict. Verified the full script end-to-end in a stubbed Node/DOM harness (this session): post_referral=255/16 (15-15/16), net_A=101/16 (6-5/16), total_fee_B=4761/1250 (3-1011/1250), net_B=56287/10000 (5-6287/10000), monthly_A=505/2 (252-1/2), monthly_B=56287/250 (225-37/250), working_capital A=35399/16 (2212-7/16) / B=24507/32 (765-27/32), winner=A -- an EXACT match to case.json.derived and sensitivity_model.py's own printed output, confirming the JS port never silently drifts from the Python model. Twist slider (packaging_cost, the case's one disclosed, author-chosen, unverifiable operational figure) ranges $3.125-$4.6875/unit (both bounds already present in case.json's own sensitivity_disclosure/derived numbers, so T1-18's CONTINUITY sweep traces them); confirmed live that the verdict flips to B exactly at the disclosed $3.8088/unit flip point (monthly_A==monthly_B there) and that A drops to $190/month (losing to B's $225-37/250) at the +50% flex endpoint -- matching sensitivity_model.py's own documented P5 finding. The Working Notebook's 6 steps (D1-D6) all self-check by calling evaluate()/working_capital() fresh at click-time (numerator-over-a-stated-denominator plus mixed-number whole/remainder fields throughout -- 16ths for D1/D2/D5-A, 1250ths for D3, 10000ths for D4-B, halves for D4 monthly-A, 250ths for D4 monthly-B, 32nds for D5-B), plus two multiple-choice checks isolating both FACILITATOR.md-documented traps (additive-vs-multiplicative surcharge application; surcharge applied to the wrong base). D6 renders a live SVG bar chart built from whatever the student typed into Steps 4/5 (not the model's own correct values), satisfying the 'built from your own D4 and D5 figures' deliverable without leaking an answer. Added a 10-term math GLOSSARY (Mixed Number/Improper Fraction/Simplify/Percent reused verbatim from cases/the-special-order and Cold Chain's own already-verified glossaries per MCS-21; Numerator/Denominator and all four multiply-a-fraction/multiply-two-fractions/multiply-a-fraction-and-mixed-number/multiply-two-mixed-numbers terms freshly live-verified HTTP 200 on khanacademy.org/mathsisfun.com 2026-09-09) exactly matching case.json.standards[]'s 10 claimed skills, plus a 5-term STORY_GLOSSARY (referral fee, Fulfilled by Amazon, Fulfilled by Merchant, fulfillment center, marketplace -- sell.amazon.com and Wikipedia links, all freshly live-verified HTTP 200 2026-09-09) covering e-commerce marketplace vocabulary, to close T1-19 and T1-21. One real CONTINUITY fix during iteration: the twist slider's first draft used integer 'eighths-of-a-dollar' values (16-56) as its min/max/value attributes, none of which trace to a literal number in case.md/case.json (T1-18 GAP) -- reworked the slider to run on the actual dollar values directly ($3.125 base to $4.6875, the case's own disclosed +50%-flex endpoint, both of which already appear in case.json's sensitivity_disclosure/derived blocks), with a fracFromDecimal() helper that converts the slider's decimal string to an exact Frac (via a fixed /10000 denominator, then gcd-reduced) before any arithmetic touches it -- so the human-facing control is decimal but the twist recompute itself stays exact-fraction throughout, same as every other step.
